Wars, Militaries and Weapons Map

Where the fighting is and was, where the armies sit, where the nuclear weapons are kept and tested, what each state spends on its forces, and the officials and companies found working for someone other than the people they answer to.

Time

Fromto

Records with no date are always shown. Dates are the source's: when a clash happened, when a base opened and closed, when a unit was formed and disbanded, when a case was registered or decided.

How dots are drawn

Filled dot: in use now, or the source records no end Ring: closed, disbanded or over, as the source records it; for the news of fighting, a report that names only a county, region or country, drawn at its seat or capital Larger dot: more people killed (armed clashes), or more events (news of fighting); darker country shading: a higher figure

Where several records share one spot, they are drawn slightly apart in a small spiral so each can be clicked; each box says so. Where dots still overlap at a zoom, a click lists every one under it.
